question: Which chemical can be used for making germ-free drinking water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CaOCl₂**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CaOCl₂ (Calcium Oxychloride)**: Commonly known as **bleaching powder**, it is widely used to disinfect or make drinking water germ-free.
 
• When added to water, it releases **chlorine**, which kills bacteria and other harmful microorganisms, making the water safe to drink.
 
• **Properties**:
 
 
• A white or light yellow powder with a chlorine-like odor.
 
• A source of chlorine when it comes into contact with water, releasing hypochlorous acid, which has strong disinfecting properties.
 
 
 
• Commonly used to disinfect and sanitize drinking water, swimming pools, and waste water.
 
• Also used as a bleaching agent in the textile and paper industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ca(OH)₂ (Calcium Hydroxide)
 
 
• Common Name: Slaked Lime
 
• Properties:
 
 
• A white, powdery, alkaline compound that is slightly soluble in water, forming a solution known as limewater.
 
• It has a high pH, making it a strong base.
 
 
 
 
 
• NaOH (Sodium Hydroxide)
 
 
• Common Name: Caustic Soda or Lye
 
• Properties:
 
 
• A highly caustic, corrosive, and water-soluble base that forms an alkaline solution in water.
 
• Very effective at breaking down organic matter, which is why it’s used in cleaning products.
 
 
 
 
 
• NH₄OH (Ammonium Hydroxide)
 
 
• Common Name: Ammonia Solution
 
• Properties:
 
• A clear, colourless liquid with a strong, pungent odour.
 
• Alkaline in nature, though not as strong as NaOH.
